WELLINGTON, New Zealand (AP) — India captain Shubman Gill has won the toss and chosen to bowl in the first cricket test against New Zealand at the Basin Reserve as the tourists are bolstered by the return of star pacer Jasprit Bumrah, who will play his first test in a year.
 The India lineup includes four fast bowlers with Bumrah supported by Anshul Kamboj, Prasidh Krishna, Akash Deep and the spinner Washington Sundar.
 Advertisement Advertisement Advertisement Wicketkeeper batters Rishabh Pant and Dhruv Jurel both will play but Pant will keep wicket.
 New Zealand also has gone for four seamers: Matt Henry, Kyle Jamieson, Jacob Duffy and Nathan Smith. Devon Conway and Rachin Ravindra return from injury to bolster the batting lineup.
 Spin allrounder Mitchell Santner is unavailable with a hand injury sustained in the last match of the recent one-day international series.
 The pitch at the Basin Reserve has been covered because of rain in recent days and again last night. When the covers were withdrawn on the morning of the first day, the pitch was green and lightly grassed.
 Advertisement Advertisement Advertisement But conditions might not be as favorable to seamers early on as the appearance of the pitch might suggest. The pitch might not provide pace and bounce until it dries and the initial moisture or softness is reduced.
 The average first innings score at the Basin Reserve is 313.
 The weather is sunny with a slight, cool southerly breeze. No rain is forecast during the test match.
 India has the chance to avenge its 3-0 series loss to New Zealand at home in 2024. But India hasn't won a test in New Zealand since 2009 when it achieved its first series victory in New Zealand in 41 years.
 In series in 2013 and 2019, India failed to win a test. It's only win at the Basin Reserve came on its inaugural tour to New Zealand in 1968.
 Advertisement Advertisement Advertisement The match marks the start of a series of six tests in 51 days for New Zealand; two against India, then four against Australia in Australia.
 New Zealand currently sits atop the World Test Championship table after six tests while India is fourth after 11 tests.
 ___
 Lineups:
 New Zealand: Tom Latham (captain), Devon Conway, Henry Nicholls, Rachin Ravindra, Daryl Mitchell, Tom Blundell, Glenn Phillips, Nathan Smith, Kyle Jamieson, Matt Henry, Jacob Duffy
 India: Yashasvi Jaiswal, K.L. Rahul, Devdutt Padikkal, Shubman Gill (captain), Rishabh Pant, Washington Sundar, Dhruv Jurel, Akash Deep, Anshul Kamboj, Jasprit Bumrah, Prasidh Krishna
